newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau question suspects after anti-triad sweep.
newsitem.headline: Macau question suspects after anti-triad sweep.

text.p: Macau police said on Tuesday they had questioned three people picked up in a sweep of suspected triad gangster hideouts across the Portuguese-ruled enclave.
A police source told Reuters that none of the three, which included one woman, had yet been charged.
Police raided 15 flats on Monday in an offensive against the secret criminal societies. The latest crackdown was sparked by a spate of gangland killings and firebombings.
Most of the flats were located in a plush residential estate where police seized documents and a number of cars.
Police also broke into what they described as an "underground wharf" and seized about 50,000 cartons of contraband cigarettes worth US$750,000.
Police sources said the wharf was built illegally under a beach-front villa, believed to be owned by a senior leader of the so-called "14 K", a powerful triad gang.
A police spokesman said the operation was directed against triads in general, not against any particular triad organisation.
The territory, famed for its casinos, reverts to China in 1999 and has been rocked by growing gangland violence, muggings, robberies and drive-by shootings in recent months.
